categories.name: 12 Levels
categories.rules:
Play the game: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1P-pBVhjmqKvxZfHVrzmfbATM9F9k-sox/view?usp=sharing

12 Levels: Beat the 12 default levels in the game as fast as possible.

Time starts on first input in level 1.

Time ends when you activate the goal on Level 12.

Times under 4:00 will include milliseconds.

Times under 3:00 will be retimed and rounded up to the nearest possible decimal at 31 fps (if needed) to ensure accuracy and consistency.

Proof Standards:

All proof standards require the standards from the previous tiers as well (i.e while it is not explicitly stated that any sub 3 12L run must have in-game sound, it is required for any sub 4 run).

Any submitted time: Must have some form of video evidence of a complete run with no edits, cuts, or significant portions of lag.

Sub 4:00: Must have a complete video with acceptable video quality (preferably at least 720p 30fps) and in game sound (music is not required).

Sub 3:00: Must have at least **ONE** of the following: an input display/face or handcam (face/handcam preferred) **OR** the upload of the full, unedited session of your PB/livestream vod of your PB (livestream preferred).

Sub 2:50: Must have at least **TWO** of the following: an input display/face or handcam (face/handcam preferred) **OR** the upload of the full, unedited session of your PB/livestream vod of your PB (livestream preferred) **OR** a desktop/task manager check at the end of your run, i.e scrolling through your task manager and showing your desktop taskbar to show that you have no unusual programs open/active that would assist in your run, and opening any active AutoHotkey (or similar programs) scripts.

Sub 2:40: Must have **ALL THREE** of the previously discussed proof checks.

Sub 2:35: **Must have some sort of external handcam.**

Please note that we may request additional proof (such as LiveSplit files) not mentioned here in some circumstances.

Example task manager check: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UyZu_w5AK5M

Sub 4:00: Must have **ALL THREE** of the previously discussed proof checks.

Sub 3:55: **Must have some sort of external handcam.**

runList.comment:
FIRST EVER 2:2X AND FINAL 10-SECOND BARRIER! This time means so much to me and it's still hard to believe that I actually achieved this. This run features all of the hard strats I've done in runs and ends it all off with Apollo 11 (11.097 train), which on its own, is 19 frame perfects. This train saved 3 seconds over my 2:32.581 FWR, which directly opened the door to achieving 2:2x. Regardless, this run still had 1 mistake in it, and that was by missing the first frame perfect of 3x choker in level 12, which costed about 0.6 seconds. If it weren't for that mistake, this run would have been a 2:29.323, which is only 2 frames off of an absolutely perfect run for my strats. Although the quest for sub 2:3x is now over, this run still has some timesave, and some extra strats can still be implemented to bring this even lower. Knowing this, I may return to this category some day, but for now, I am entirely satisfied with this run. Huge shoutouts to the Red Ball community, especially those who always believed in me and motivated me to achieve this unbelievable run.

Desktop Only Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WvaKgCeamkw

Pulsoid Heartrate Statistics: https://pulsoid.net/stream-report/niftski-CFs9g

I am in absolute disbelief this happened. I started playing Red Ball for fun on December 26th, 2022, and after almost 2 years since my first run, I have finally achieved a dream of mine, getting the 12 Levels World Record. I was going for [2:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0r88uedkO2I&t=153s) but i lost 0.2 seconds from a slow 10 ending which is why this is barely not a [2:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0r88uedkO2I&t=153s). Thank you to the entire Red Ball Community for always motivating me, you guys are absolutely the best. For now, I am absolutely satisfied with this run, but I may potentially return to this game one day for [2:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0r88uedkO2I&t=152s), but for now others can try to beat this run if they want. Just know that this is easily the best Speedrunning accomplishment of my life.

On top of all that, this run was the first ever 2:35 pace to train, and in fact was the best pace to train by over half a second, making it even more insane to me that I clutched it out.

I'm completely finished with this category for now although I may return for sub 2:35 some day, and I look forward to seeing others trying to beat this time in the future!

I can't believe I got this. Since 2021, this has been a very distant pipedream for me. Back then, I got my first sub 4, a 3:38.323. Then in 2023 I was drawn back to the game. First I got a 3:18.000, then a 3:12.871, then 3:09.516, and finally 3:07.419, saved by PBird. But I got on an insane run. It had almost zero mistakes and was on 2:55 pace into 11, where I unfortunately messed up PBird, still getting a 3:03.742. Now a year later I came back to the game. I played for 3 weeks without much happening, in that time i only got one run to 11 on pace. Then yesterday, I got a HUGE spike in motivation to get sub 3. I played for almost five hours that day, getting 2 PBs. The first was a small one of 3:03.290 which messed up the stair jump in 12. I then got on a run that was easy sub 3 pace past the superbounce in 10, that choked the ending. Still it was possible. After nailing PBird and 12, I thought it was fast enough but it got 3:00.323. Now today i got this run. Not only is this sub 3, it's TRULY satisfying. I was under a second behind my 3:03.742 into 11, and that run is still my best pace ever. I got PBird and managed to close out the run, smashing the sub 3 barrier with a 2:56.516. I am done with this game forever. (for now)

Tally Hall is an American rock band formed in December 2002 and based in Ann Arbor, Michigan. The band is known for upbeat melodies and whimsical lyrics. The members originally described their musical style as "wonky rock," later redefining their sound as "fə-blōō", in an effort to not let their music be defined by any particular genres after people began to start defining the characteristics of "wonky rock".[1]

Tally Hall has five members, each of them distinguished by the color of their neckties: guitarist Rob Cantor (yellow), guitarist Joe Hawley (red), drummer Ross Federman (gray), keyboardist Andrew Horowitz (green), and bassist Zubin Sedghi (blue). Every member has provided vocals for the band.

Once under the Atlantic Records recording label, Tally Hall was, again, signed to indie label Quack!Media,[2] who previously helped finance and nationally distribute their debut studio album, Marvin's Marvelous Mechanical Museum. They released their second album, Good & Evil, on June 21, 2011.[3]

Tally Hall also provided the vocals and music for all of the songs in Happy Monster Band, a children's television series that aired on Playhouse Disney.
